Weeknight tomato and bean stew

By Rosa Klein · Updated 8 October · 45 minutes

This is the kind of dinner that starts with an onion and ends with something deeply savoury, without asking you to babysit a pot for hours. The beans do most of the work.

Use a good tinned tomato and a generous amount of olive oil. The stew is even better the next day, so it is worth making a double batch on Sunday.

Ingredients

  • Two tablespoons of olive oil
  • One large yellow onion, diced
  • Three cloves of garlic, sliced
  • Two tins of cannellini beans
  • One tin of whole peeled tomatoes
  • A small bunch of flat-leaf parsley

Method

  1. Warm the olive oil in a heavy pot over medium heat, then cook the onion with a pinch of salt until it is soft and translucent, about eight minutes.
  2. Add the garlic and cook for one more minute, stirring so it does not brown, then tip in the tomatoes and break them up with a wooden spoon.
  3. Drain and rinse the beans, add them to the pot with a splash of water, and simmer uncovered for twenty minutes until the liquid thickens around the beans.
  4. Taste and adjust the salt, scatter the chopped parsley over the top, and serve with toasted bread or rice.

Cook's notes

If you have a parmesan rind, drop it in with the tomatoes and fish it out before serving.

Reviews

Marta — 4 stars

Made this on a Tuesday after work and it took exactly as long as promised. I added a pinch of chilli flakes and it was even better the next day for lunch.

Dev — 5 stars

I was sceptical about the amount of olive oil but it really does make the dish. My kids asked for it again the following week, which never happens.

Lena — 3 stars

Good base recipe, though I found it needed quite a lot more salt than written. The timing for the beans was accurate in my oven-safe pot.
